newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: EC's Santer says backs Italian efforts to join EMU.
newsitem.headline: EC's Santer says backs Italian efforts to join EMU.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Thursday he backed Italy's efforts to meet the Maastricht criteria for a single European currency but declined to comment on the country's chances of success.
"I support all efforts that various member states, including Italy, are making to meet the criteria. I welcome (Italian Prime Minister Romano) Prodi's efforts," Santer told a news conference.
"But we should not speculate now on which states will fulfil the criteria. I just hope that it will be a large number, especially when one considers the efforts they are making," he continued.

He sidestepped questions about the extent of opposition within the European Union to the lira's early return to the European Exchange Rate Mechanism - the precursor to a single currency. The lira left the ERM following a speculative attack in 1992.
Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky said it was in the interests of all EU members to see as many countries as possible participating in a single currency.
"And Italy is one of those countries," he said.
Italy is one of Austria's major trading partners.
"If not everyone makes the 1999 start then it is a question of setting a transition period. We want to rule out competitive devaluations," Vranitzky said. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
